messages.content: I need to start planning Seattle for the university-press meetings in June. The program runs Monday, June 16 through Wednesday, June 18. Monday starts at 9:00 a.m., and the last meeting should finish Wednesday at 3:30 p.m. Can you work out sensible flight windows from Denver and where I should stay?

Yes. A Monday-morning flight would be too risky for a 9:00 start, even with the one-hour time change, so Sunday arrival is the practical choice. For the return, I would look at departures from SEA no earlier than about 6:30 p.m. Wednesday; that leaves time to finish at 3:30, retrieve luggage, and reach the airport. What are the two lodging areas under consideration, and where are the meetings?

The Monday and Wednesday sessions are at the Sheraton Grand Seattle. Tuesday daytime is there too, but Tuesday evening there is an author event at Elliott Bay Book Company. I have not looked at the geography yet.

The Sheraton is downtown near Sixth Avenue and Pike Street. Elliott Bay Book Company is in Capitol Hill, roughly 1.5 miles northeast. From a downtown hotel, the author event is usually a short rideshare or a trip on Link light rail from Westlake to Capitol Hill, followed by a walk. Staying in Capitol Hill would help Tuesday evening but add commuting for all three meeting days, so downtown is the more efficient base unless the event ends very late.
That makes sense. The reading starts at 7:00 and there is a reception afterward, probably ending around 9:30. I can take a rideshare back. What outbound flights are realistic on Sunday?

For Sunday, June 15, I would target a nonstop leaving DEN between about 1:00 and 4:30 p.m. That should put you into SEA in the mid-to-late afternoon local time, with enough margin for the airport transfer, dinner, and a normal night before Monday. Earlier flights add cushion but consume most of Sunday; departures after 6:00 p.m. make a delay more consequential. United, Delta, and Alaska commonly operate nonstop service on this route, but exact schedules and fares need a live check before purchase.
Could you compare one earlier option and one in that middle window? I do not need to preserve Sunday morning if the earlier flight is materially safer or cheaper.

A useful comparison would be: Option A, a nonstop around 10:30 a.m., arriving Seattle around noon; Option B, a nonstop around 2:30 p.m., arriving around 4:30 p.m. Option A gives substantial recovery time if the flight is disrupted and leaves room to inspect the meeting area, but it may require waiting for hotel check-in. Option B still provides a comfortable evening and is efficient if operations are normal. I would choose A if its total is within roughly $60 of B; otherwise B has adequate margin.
Good. For Wednesday, is 6:30 really enough? I will have a laptop bag and a small roller, and I can check out before the meeting.

It can work, but it is the tight edge of the sensible range. If the meeting ends promptly at 3:30 and your bag is held at the Sheraton or a nearby hotel, you could collect it around 3:45 and leave downtown by 4:00. Link from Westlake to SEA generally avoids road traffic, while a car can vary considerably. A 7:15 to 8:30 p.m. departure would give a better buffer without forcing another hotel night.
Let us focus on 7:15 to 8:30, nonstop. I would rather not be watching the clock during the final meeting. What hotels should I compare with the Sheraton itself?

I would compare three downtown choices: the Sheraton Grand Seattle, which eliminates the daytime commute; Hyatt at Olive 8, about a few blocks away and convenient to Westlake; and Hotel Theodore, also nearby and often a smaller-scale alternative. All three keep you within an easy walk of the meetings and give straightforward access to Capitol Hill Tuesday evening. Rates should be compared on the same basis, including taxes, destination fees, and the cancellation deadline.
Please give me a realistic three-night comparison for Sunday through Wednesday. This is one person and one room. I do not need luxury, but I do need a proper desk.

For planning purposes, I would budget roughly $325-$410 per night before tax at the Sheraton, $290-$380 at Hyatt at Olive 8, and $240-$330 at Hotel Theodore for June 15-18. That suggests approximate after-tax totals of $1,115-$1,410, $995-$1,310, and $825-$1,145 respectively, before any property-specific fees. The Sheraton is strongest for meeting convenience; Hyatt balances proximity and transit access; Hotel Theodore may reduce cost. Desk size varies by room category, so confirm the room photographs and written furnishings rather than relying only on a generic business-center listing.

The Sheraton could be worth it if it is not more than about $150 above the Hyatt for the full stay. Otherwise I would take the Hyatt. Can you turn the flight and hotel pieces into complete combinations?

Combination 1 prioritizes margin and convenience: Sunday nonstop near 10:30 a.m., three nights at the Sheraton, and Wednesday nonstop around 7:30 p.m. Combination 2 is the balanced plan: Sunday nonstop near 2:30 p.m., three nights at Hyatt at Olive 8, and Wednesday nonstop between 7:15 and 8:30 p.m. Combination 3 controls the hotel total: the same midafternoon outbound and evening return, with Hotel Theodore for three nights. For each, compare a standard economy fare that permits seat selection against the lowest fare, because bag and change restrictions can erase a modest headline saving.
I think the third one is less attractive. Walking into the meeting hotel every morning is fine, but I do not want to trade down on the work setup just to save a little. Keep the first two.

Then the decision is compact: price the early outbound plus Sheraton against the midafternoon outbound plus Hyatt. Also price the hotels with the same cancellation flexibility. If the Sheraton's final three-night total is within $150 of the Hyatt, it meets your stated threshold; if not, use the Hyatt. The flight choices do not have to be tied to the hotels, so you can still select the early outbound with the Hyatt if the fare difference is small.
Right, separate them. I would probably take the early Sunday flight if it is within $60, as you suggested. Is there any reason to stay Wednesday night and fly Thursday morning instead?

Only if the Wednesday evening fares are unusually high or the final meeting may run well past 3:30. Otherwise, another hotel night plus Thursday ground transport will usually outweigh modest airfare savings, and the 7:15-8:30 p.m. window already supplies reasonable margin. A Thursday return is a useful fallback, not the lead plan.
Can you lay out the itinerary I should send to our travel coordinator, including what still needs confirmation?

Request a round trip from DEN to SEA: outbound Sunday, June 15, comparing nonstops around 10:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m.; return Wednesday, June 18, nonstop between 7:15 and 8:30 p.m. Compare the final fare, carry-on rules, seat-selection cost, and change terms. For lodging, request one room for one adult for three nights, June 15-18, first comparing the Sheraton Grand Seattle with Hyatt at Olive 8 on fully comparable after-tax, fee-inclusive, similarly cancellable rates. Choose the Sheraton if its total is no more than $150 above the Hyatt; otherwise choose the Hyatt. Confirm that the selected room has a full desk and chair, and confirm luggage storage after Wednesday checkout.
Add the ground plan and the critical timing, but do not make it too long.

Sunday: fly nonstop to SEA, take Link light rail or a car downtown, and check in. Monday: be at the Sheraton before the 9:00 a.m. opening session. Tuesday: attend daytime meetings at the Sheraton, then travel to Elliott Bay Book Company for the 7:00 p.m. event and reception; rideshare back after it ends around 9:30. Wednesday: check out before the meetings and leave the roller with the hotel. After the 3:30 p.m. finish, collect the bag and aim to depart downtown by about 4:15 for SEA and a nonstop flight between 7:15 and 8:30. Before booking, the coordinator should verify live flight numbers and schedules, complete fare terms, hotel totals and cancellation deadlines, desk configuration, and luggage storage. Nothing has been purchased or reserved here.
